sources.entry: auto-mcs - Cross-platform Minecraft server manager. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Python

summary.one_liner: auto-mcs is a cross-platform Minecraft server manager that handles creating, importing, running, and maintaining Minecraft servers for playing with friends.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a desktop app for creating a Minecraft server in under a minute, with preconfigured templates or manual options for distribution, version, and whitelist. It can import an existing server by selecting its root folder, and it can use modpacks from a built-in Modrinth browser or from imported .zip/.mrpack files. It advertises a mod and plugin manager with Modrinth search, installation, and updates, plus automatic server installation, updates, and backup management. Other listed features include a custom console with a scripting API and built-in IDE, an access control page for operators, bans, and the whitelist, a server.properties editor, crash detection with reports, and a playit.gg integration for hosting without port forwarding. The README says it supports Paper, Purpur, Fabric, Quilt, NeoForge, Forge, Spigot, CraftBukkit, and Vanilla.
use_cases: host a Minecraft server for friends without port forwarding
import an existing Minecraft server and manage it
install and update Minecraft mods or plugins from Modrinth
run a modpack from a .mrpack or .zip file
automatically back up a Minecraft world
manage operators, bans, and whitelist from one page
how_to_run: Download the latest version of auto-mcs from the website or GitHub
Extract the .zip file to a location of your choice
On Linux, run chmod +x auto-mcs if needed to make the binary executable
Launch auto-mcs; no installation is required
Create a new server or import an existing one, then click launch
notable: Playit.gg integration for hosting without port forwarding
Modrinth-based mod, plugin, and modpack browser with updates
Built-in scripting API and IDE for the server console, compatible with Vanilla
Imports existing servers by copying them and making a backup, leaving the original untouched
Crash detection with an accessible report
caveats: README says the project is relatively new and many things may change during development
Some features and documentation are referenced on an external website and Docker Hub rather than fully in the README
Donations are requested to support continued development
